title: What the federal papers on the Medi-Cal deferrals say
question: What did the federal government publish about the 2026 deferrals and the rules on federal money for people covered only by the State?
finding: The HHS notice of July 21, 2026 puts the California deferral at about $867.5 million (Minnesota $199 million), the same day as the deferral letter for the quarter ended 31 March 2026. The April 2026 guidance repeats the $1.8 billion of questionable claims across eight States with State-only programs, and the September 2025 letter ends federal money in health-plan payments for this group from January 2027. The September 2025 letter describes the 2024 audit as covering an 18-month period, but the dates it gives (October 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019) span 9 months.
how: Read from the three PDFs supplied (text extracted with pdftotext); every figure and date is matched in the text by the script.
limits: A deferral holds money back while the State documents its claims; it is not a finding that the claims were wrong. The guidance letters set rules for all States and name California only as an example. The press notice is the agency's own description.

doc.t: HHS Defers More Than $1 Billion in Medicaid Payments to California, Minnesota Pending Review of High-Risk Claims

rows.said: The federal agency deferred about $867.5 million of federal Medicaid payments to California after reviewing claims for in-home care programs and other claims; it calls them deferrals, not permanent cuts.

doc.t: State Health Official letter 26-001: implementation of section 71109, alien Medicaid eligibility

rows.said: From 1 October 2026 federal matching funds are limited to listed immigration categories; the agency's review of eight states with State-only programs found about $1.8 billion of questionable expenditures.

doc.t: State Medicaid Director letter 25-003: managed care payments and emergency medical condition coverage

rows.said: Monthly payments to health plans can no longer carry federal emergency-Medicaid money for people ineligible for full benefits; State-only services need separate contracts; enforcement from the first rating period a year on (1 January 2027 for calendar-year plans).
Cites the inspector general's May 2024 finding that California improperly claimed $52.7 million over 18 months, October 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019; that span is 9 months.

sources.t: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, press release, 21 July 2026
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, State Medicaid Director letter SMD 25-003, 30 September 2025
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, State Health Official letter SHO 26-001, 8 April 2026
